mutants.name: M1-behind-not-checked
mutants.why: ignoring the behind count means a checkout 1 behind origin passes as current — test 2 asserts (False, '1 behind / 0 ahead')

mutants.name: M2-ahead-not-checked
mutants.why: ignoring the ahead count means a checkout 1 ahead of origin passes as current — test 3 asserts (False, '0 behind / 1 ahead')

mutants.name: M3-failed-fetch-returns-true
mutants.why: swallowing a non-zero fetch exit and returning True violates the fail-closed contract — test 4 asserts (False, 'fetch failed: ...')
mutants.replacement: return (True, f"M3: fetch failed but swallowed: {first_err}")

mutants.name: M4-push-skipped-in-teardown
mutants.why: without the push call, origin/main does not advance after merge — test 7 asserts origin sha equals project sha

mutants.name: M5-rejected-push-swallowed
mutants.why: if the rejected push is not turned into a WorktreeTeardownError, the worktree is silently removed — test 8 asserts WorktreeTeardownError with 'worktree_teardown_push_rejected'

mutants.name: M6-wire-a-writes-no-hold
mutants.why: if the stale-checkout hold_reason is wrong, the sidecar check in test 9 fails — test 9 asserts hold_reason == 'stale-checkout'

mutants.name: M7-push-uses-force
mutants.why: a --force push overwrites origin unconditionally — test 10 asserts '--force' is absent from _push_main source

mutants.name: M8-wire-c-push-rejected-not-retryable
mutants.why: without 'worktree_teardown_push_rejected' in the retry allowlist, a push-rejected failure is not retried — test 13 asserts the teardown retry succeeds and clears the failure

mutants.name: M9-head-check-removed
mutants.why: without the HEAD-branch guard a side-branch checkout is not detected as stale — test 14 asserts (False, 'HEAD is on side, not main')
mutants.replacement: if False:  # M9: HEAD check removed
